key: I form the light, and create darkness; I make peace, and create evil; I am the LORD, that doeth all these things.
s: Closing the LORD’s address to Cyrus, which denies any God beside Him, the verse pairs opposites; Ibn Ezra, on 45:7, takes ‘create’ as decree, darkness as mere absence of light, and evil as war or sickness, named because God strengthens Cyrus and weakens Babylon’s king.

evidence.gloss: [On ‘and creates darkness’:] from the root of creation, in the sense of decree, for darkness is nothing, only the absence of light … [on ‘and creates evil’:] evil is war, the opposite of peace, or sickness in a man’s body, which fights against his constitution; and he mentions this in this passage because He will strengthen Cyrus, the reverse of the king of Babylon (Friedlander: strengthen Cyrus and weaken the king of Babylon).

reason: CORRECTED for the critic’s one problem, which holds: the context clause was a participial fragment with no subject or main verb. It now reads ‘Closing the LORD’s address to Cyrus, which denies any God beside Him, the verse pairs opposites;’ (the verse pairs light and darkness, peace and evil, as Ibn Ezra’s own first lemma says, הזכיר דבר והפכו). To stay at the cap the reading was trimmed without changing its content: ‘darkness being only absence of light’ became ‘darkness as mere absence of light’, ‘the evil’ became ‘evil’.
